sentences.text: GNAO1-related disease (neurodevelopmental disorder with involuntary movements) looks similar clinically but shares no supported mechanism, so it is excluded.
CACNA1A-related disease (migraine, familial hemiplegic, 1) overlaps only weakly at Regulation of insulin secretion, a related process but a different step.
SLC2A1-related disease (hereditary cryohydrocytosis with reduced stomatin) overlaps only weakly at Regulation of insulin secretion, a related process but a different step.

GRIN1-related disease (neurodevelopmental disorder with or without hyperkinetic movements and seizures, autosomal dominant) overlaps only weakly at Neurexins and neuroligins, a related process but a different step.

Variant evidence differs (V=0): STXBP1 (loss_of_function), “De novo loss of function mutations in STXBP1 are a relatively common cause of epilepsy and intellectual disability (ID).”; CACNA1A-related disease (migraine, familial hemiplegic, 1) (gain_of_function), “Two variants known leading to gain of function (GOF) were found in 5 patients.”.

Variant evidence differs (V=0): STXBP1 (loss_of_function), “De novo loss of function mutations in STXBP1 are a relatively common cause of epilepsy and intellectual disability (ID).”; GRIN1-related disease (neurodevelopmental disorder with or without hyperkinetic movements and seizures, autosomal dominant) (gain_of_function), “including variants in the pore-forming region, linker regions and elsewhere that uniformly increase NMDA receptor-mediated charge transfer.”.
Contradictory evidence is indexed: “We found no correlation between severity of seizures and severity of ID”.
Contradictory evidence is indexed: “or between mutation type and seizure characteristics or cognitive outcome.”.

Contradictory evidence is indexed: “None of the recurrent variants were significantly associated with distinct electroclinical syndromes, single phenotypic features, or showed overall clinical similarity”.

Ingo Helbig (The Children's Hospital of Philadelphia) has published on both STXBP1- and STX1B-related disease.
Ingrid E Scheffer (The University of Melbourne) has published on both STXBP1- and CACNA1A-related disease.

## What differs and must be verified
GNAO1-related disease (neurodevelopmental disorder with involuntary movements) looks similar clinically but shares no supported mechanism, so it is excluded. [f94ad5494a3e9ab8]
CACNA1A-related disease (migraine, familial hemiplegic, 1) overlaps only weakly at Regulation of insulin secretion, a related process but a different step. [34c9bc447921f8cb, 187be2699f417de6, 3a40a3f53a18b664]
SLC2A1-related disease (hereditary cryohydrocytosis with reduced stomatin) overlaps only weakly at Regulation of insulin secretion, a related process but a different step. [20c30f77dc2491fb, 5490966f0991bdf8, 3a40a3f53a18b664]
GRIN1-related disease (neurodevelopmental disorder with or without hyperkinetic movements and seizures, autosomal dominant) overlaps only weakly at Neurexins and neuroligins, a related process but a different step. [9b5a310872598764, 072a91fd2fdb335f, ce6dd3aad07a277e]
Variant evidence differs (V=0): STXBP1 (loss_of_function), “De novo loss of function mutations in STXBP1 are a relatively common cause of epilepsy and intellectual disability (ID).”; CACNA1A-related disease (migraine, familial hemiplegic, 1) (gain_of_function), “Two variants known leading to gain of function (GOF) were found in 5 patients.”. [9b5a310872598764, 87257c69fcfbcdad, df57b34e24ef5206, c9e703902a0fb3f5, 0211d2b50f1f9730]
Contradictory evidence is indexed: “We found no correlation between severity of seizures and severity of ID”. [b1f9e5eeafbc81d2]
